patches.reason: Set and measure PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0 inside the final credential-bearing Linux go-judge executable, because execve resets launcher-only hardening. A failed syscall/readback stops startup before main. No sandbox role or namespace/capability boundary is weakened.
patches.licenseImpact: New Code Startrack Linux startup integration source is separately Apache-2.0 attributed; original upstream files and MIT license remain unchanged.
patches.upgradeCondition: Retain until a reviewed exact upstream executable measures nondumpability after exec. Verify actual sibling /proc memory/environment denial and final runtime PID under the released Linux profile; portable compilation is insufficient.

patches.reason: Assemble a fixed embedded workload-only namespace guard with the pinned Elastic API and supply it through both existing linuxcontainer builder paths and ExecveParam.Seccomp. Preserve the unchanged broad init whitelist and trusted clone3(CLONE_INTO_CGROUP) setup; only workload unshare/setns, namespace clone flags and clone3 are restricted. Workload clone3 returns ENOSYS for libc fallback; conditional clone is terminal to avoid pinned assembler accumulator fall-through changing ordinary syscalls. Refuse disabled or caller-replaced init policies.
patches.licenseImpact: Modified upstream env source remains MIT with prominent Code Startrack comments and byte-identical upstream LICENSE/NOTICE. New fixed profile, assembler integration and inert VM regression tests are separately Apache-2.0 attributed. No custom BPF or isolation implementation is introduced.
patches.upgradeCondition: Rebase only against reviewed exact go-judge and go-sandbox pins. Inspect both builder paths, inherited init-profile identity, mature final-exec seccomp ordering, assembler argument accumulator and clone ABI. Rerun actual loader VM ordinary-syscall/clone/clone3/x32/foreign-architecture stack regressions, source/license closure and final Linux compiler/reference/validator/thread/fork/verdict/isolation matrix with at least three workload filters. Portable VM tests do not establish Linux installation or sandbox acceptance.

patches.reason: Remove only propagation-operation flags from the read-only bind remount after a successful initial private recursive bind; preserve MS_BIND, MS_RDONLY and inherited nosuid/nodev/noexec/time lock flags. AppArmor rejects the redundant propagation/remount combination. Remount failure still aborts sandbox creation.
patches.licenseImpact: Modified go-sandbox source remains MIT. Original license is retained byte-identically; source carries a prominent Code Startrack modification comment. No upstream isolation implementation is replaced.
patches.upgradeCondition: Rebase only against a reviewed exact go-sandbox pin. Recheck initial mount and namespace propagation flags, inherited statfs lock flags and remount failure behavior; qualify read-only write denial on every configured bind including nested mounts under the reviewed Linux AppArmor/capability profile.

patches.reason: Retain CAP_SETPCAP across exec only for the trusted nested namespace init so upstream keep_capability can set securebits under inherited no_new_privs. Actual prefork init had full namespace bounding capabilities but only the eight outer permitted/effective capabilities and lacked SETPCAP; its securebits transition returned EPERM. The outer capability set and AppArmor profile are unchanged, and upstream child DropCaps remains mandatory.
patches.licenseImpact: Modified go-sandbox source remains MIT with its original license retained byte-identically and a prominent Code Startrack modification comment. The reviewed upstream isolation, no_new_privs, securebits locking and child capability removal remain in place.
patches.upgradeCondition: Rebase only against a reviewed exact go-sandbox pin. Inspect startContainer, exec capability propagation, keep_capability securebits and DropCaps; qualify actual trusted-init execution, zero effective/permitted/inheritable/ambient child capabilities, measured namespace-scoped bounding set, locked securebits47 and no_new_privs1, actual capability-regain/mount/pivot_root/user-and-network-namespace denials, and credential isolation under the exact released Linux profile.

patches.reason: Supply the two zeroed CapUserData words required by Linux capability ABI v3 and pass element zero in each of the three existing CAPSET calls. The pinned single 12-byte structure let the kernel read the required second word from adjacent globals, potentially failing capability removal with EPERM. This repairs the existing intended zero-drop semantics without changing securebits, bounding-set, credential, namespace or seccomp policy.
patches.licenseImpact: Modified go-sandbox source remains MIT; original license stays byte-identical and a prominent Code Startrack comment identifies the ABI correction. Mature upstream isolation and failure propagation remain in place.
patches.upgradeCondition: Rebase only against a reviewed exact go-sandbox pin. Verify the Linux capability header version, full kernel data size, all CAPSET call sites and zero-array bytes in the actual Linux ELF; rerun child capability, securebits, no_new_privs, capability-regain denial, compiler/reference/validator and full sandbox verdict/security qualification.

patches.reason: Pass the already-supported execCmd.Seccomp filter to forkexec.Runner.Seccomp using existing Filter.SockFprog, activating the mature post-setup workload installation path. The exact upstream had deliberately set this field nil; the broad inherited init policy remains installed, trusted cgroup/namespace setup and DropCaps remain unchanged.
patches.licenseImpact: Modified go-sandbox source remains MIT with original license byte-identical and a prominent Code Startrack comment. This reconnects existing mature filter plumbing and does not introduce custom BPF, new sandbox machinery or outer profile/capability changes.
patches.upgradeCondition: Rebase only against a reviewed exact go-sandbox pin. Inspect ExecveParam/execCmd serialization, SockFprog lifetime and existing forkexec filter installation after trusted namespace/cgroup and capability removal. Verify nonempty workload guard on ordinary and clone3 cgroup paths; rerun actual source loader VM and complete exact-image Linux isolation, fork/thread, compiler/reference/validator and verdict qualification.
